readings: out is a combinational function of the current state (out=1 in B, out=0 in A), so it changes immediately when the state changes, including during asynchronous reset.
out is a registered signal updated on the clock edge, so it is delayed by one clock cycle relative to the state and may not change immediately during reset unless explicitly reset.
During areset=1, state is forced to B, so out becomes 1 asynchronously (if combinational) or is asynchronously reset to 1.
During areset=1, out is not affected by the reset (if registered without reset), so it holds its previous value or 0, and only updates on the next clock edge.
State updates on the rising edge of clk (posedge).
State updates on the falling edge of clk (negedge).
If areset is never asserted, the initial state at power-up is undefined (e.g., X in simulation, unpredictable in hardware).
If areset is never asserted, the initial state is assumed to be B (out=1).
